headline: Investor Michael Burry expects the Trump administration to do everything it can to protect the AI boom, while valuation expert Aswath Damodaran keeps most of his new money in cash.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: two prominent market voices on the AI-boom risk, but they are opinions.
importance_line: People whose savings or pensions sit in big tech shares would be hit if these warnings prove right, but they are the personal views of two investors, not evidence of what will happen.
summary: Stocktwits reports, in a story Yahoo Finance carries, that investor Michael Burry wrote on Substack that the administration will "pull out all the stops" to protect the AI boom, though backstopping trillions would carry "epic moral hazard" and have limits, and that valuation expert Aswath Damodaran holds five of the seven biggest US tech stocks but has put most new money in cash, warning of "accounting and market carnage" if AI fails to deliver. These are personal opinions, and the same article quotes a more upbeat Goldman Sachs strategist who expects strong tech earnings to continue.
notes: Our 27 Sep to 1 Oct 2026 editions carried earlier Burry warnings. No investment advice; no tickers.
